summary: A bilingual (English/Japanese) project page for a typeface that fuses Braille dots with Latin and Katakana letterforms so sighted and blind readers share one text. It argues inclusion rather than legibility metrics: a photo of a finger reading embossed type, a 'Braille + character → Braille Neue' equation, real signage and exhibition case studies, partner logos and press. The font itself appears only in images; the page is set in Poppins and Noto Sans JP, and licensing is by contact form.

instances.look: Full-screen photo, darkened to 70%, of a white surface printed with blue Braille Neue words with raised black dots, a fingertip touching them; 'Character with Braille.' in white Poppins at 72px left of centre with the Japanese line '点字と文字が一体になった、目でも指でも読める書体。' under it; a transparent top bar with 'Braille Neue' and 8 anchor links
instances.ux: Anchor nav to About, Project Movie, Typeface, Case Study, Collaborator, Media, Reference, Contact; headline fades in after load
instances.learn: For a tactile typeface, the hero photo should show a hand reading it: the image explains 'readable by eye and by finger' before any copy
